transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-18
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Priya Desai (Redwood AE), Marcus Hill (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Cascade - Head of Data), Mark Hsu (Cascade - ML Eng), Danielle Park (Cascade - Product)
---
Auto-summary (brief): Walkthrough of Redwood Eval/Optimize features focused on prompt-set driven regression detection, alerting, and A/B comparisons for ranking/generation use-cases. Customer to provide prompt corpus and infra contacts.
---
00:00:00 Priya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Priya with Redwood, this is Marcus our solutions engineer. How are you all doing?
00:00:06 Lena: Doing well, thanks. Excited to see how you flag regressions — we've had a few nasty shifts after rollouts.
00:00:12 Marcus: Great — we'll dive into the console and then the eval API, show A/B compare flows and the alerting rules. Quick note: I'm going to demo with a sample ecommerce prompt set similar to what you described.
00:00:24 Danielle: Perfect. Our main goals are detectable regression, fast A/B feedback, and minimal infra changes. We'll also need to check security.
00:00:33 Priya: Noted. Quick qualification — can you remind us of your stack? Hosting, model approach, any private deployment constraints?
00:00:40 Mark: We're mixed. Prod is in GCP, model inference today is via Anthropic hosted endpoints for chat and a small on-prem transformer for some sensitive flows. We want to reduce latency in checkout flows and detect any semantic regressions after prompt or model updates.
00:00:56 Marcus: Got it — so a hybrid setup. Do you have a preference for hosted vs dedicated vs private?
00:01:02 Lena: For initial eval hosted is fine, but for anything handling PII we need VPC or private. We are SOC2 in progress and will need audit logs.
00:01:10 Priya: That's common. Redwood supports Hosted API for quick evals and Private/VPC for later stages. We also include audit logs and KMS integrations for private deploys. We'll share the security packet.
00:01:22 Mark: How do you store prompt sets and telemetry? Do you persist user inputs?
00:01:27 Marcus: By default telemetry for evals is stored in the customer's account — retention is configurable. For sensitive data you can opt-out or encrypt at-rest with your KMS if using Private.
00:01:36 Priya: Ok, let's get into the demo. I'll pass to Marcus to share the console and the A/B flow.
00:01:42 Marcus: Sharing screen now... (brief pause, screen share)
00:02:10 Marcus: This is the Eval console home — top shows recent runs, health pulse, and active alerts. I'm going to open a prompt-set we've prepared called "checkout-affordance" — it contains 240 canonical user prompts and several rubrics.
00:02:24 Marcus: You'll notice we surface per-prompt metrics: pass/fail, BLEU-ish style similarity, and custom judgments. We also have automatic baselining which computes rolling windows.
00:02:39 Danielle: Are those rubrics human-labeled or auto?
00:02:41 Marcus: They can be either. You can upload human labels, import eval scripts, or use automated heuristics. For your use-case we recommend a mix — a small human-labeled seed + automated checks for scale.
00:02:50 00:02:52 Mark: (interruption) How frequently do alerts fire? We had too many false positives before.
00:02:56 Marcus: Good question — alert sensitivity is configurable. We support z-score thresholds, percentage-drop rules, and can suppress alerts during canaries. You can tune per-prompt or per-metric.
00:03:08 Marcus: I'll set up an A/B comparison between model v1 (your current hosted) and v2 (candidate) — we call it a "split test". You point a subset of traffic or run an offline batch and Redwood computes pairwise comparisons and aggregate metrics.
00:03:22 Marcus: Starting an offline A/B run... selecting prompt set, choosing metrics — accuracy, semantic similarity, and a custom business rubric for 'cart abandonment risk'.
00:03:33 00:03:36 Lena: What's the unit cost for those runs? We have budget constraints.
00:03:39 Priya: For offline evals the cost is primarily token-cost + small per-run fee for compute; we can show you the price estimate before you run. For live A/B (traffic splits) it depends on host vs dedicated. We'll include cost projections in the follow-up.
00:03:53 Marcus: Ok results are in — you'll see a per-prompt diff table. Some prompts show a notable drop for v2 in the 'risk' metric. We flag regressions in red and create a prioritized problem list.
00:04:06 Mark: Can we export that into our ticketing system?
00:04:09 Marcus: Yes — we have integrations for Slack, Jira, and webhooks. You can auto-create issues for high-severity regressions.
00:04:16 00:04:20 Danielle: How do you ensure the A/B is apples-to-apples when models have different tokenization or truncation behavior?
00:04:24 Marcus: We normalize responses and apply alignment heuristics; for large differences we recommend synthetic canonicalization. Also we store raw responses to reproduce.
00:04:36 Marcus: Now I'll show regression alerting — you can create an alert rule that watches a metric over a rolling 7-day window and triggers when there's a 15% drop or a 2-sigma deviation.
00:04:48 Marcus: I'll demo with a simulated drift. (runs simulation) You can see an auto-generated incident with suggested rollback options — either fallback to a previous variant or change routing to a lower-latency variant.
00:05:00 Lena: That rollback to previous variant — is that automatic or manual?
00:05:03 Marcus: We support both. You can set an automatic policy for critical regressions or require manual approval for others.
00:05:09 Mark: Do you capture the KV cache behavior? We've seen regressions related to cached prefixes.
00:05:14 Marcus: We capture per-request context snapshots and KV cache stats. Small caveat, transcript note: sometimes KV cache gets transcribed as K V cache in older logs.
00:05:24 Marcus: Let's flip to the API — I'll show how you can programmatically push a new prompt-set and trigger an eval run. (typing)
00:05:34 00:05:38 Marcus: Example curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.infer/v1/evals -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"prompt_set_id":"checkout-affordance" ... }' — That will enqueue a run and return a run_id.
00:05:50 Mark: Nice — we can hook that to our CI so every PR that touches prompts triggers a run?
00:05:54 Marcus: Exactly. CI integration is common: run per-PR checks and gate merges on no-regression.
00:06:00 Priya: Wanted to call out the Eval exports — CSVs, JSONL with raw responses, and an audit trail. Security wise we can filter out PII fields before storage.
00:06:11 Lena: How does data residency work for hosted accounts? We need EU-only for some flows.
00:06:15 Marcus: We provide region pinning for hosted — EU-only buckets and compute. For fully on-prem or VPC, data never leaves your network.
00:06:22 Danielle: Good. Can you show the alert configuration UI?
00:06:25 Marcus: Sure — opening Alerts -> New Rule. You pick scope (prompt-level or global), metric, threshold type, and actions. I'll create a rule scoped to 'checkout-affordance' where semantic-similarity drops 10% vs baseline.
00:06:38 Marcus: Now I'll simulate a drift and show the notification — Slack webhook example fires and we auto-create a Jira ticket with attachments.
00:06:48 00:06:52 Mark: (comment) We want to be careful about false positives. Can you do an alert that only fires if both semantic-similarity and a business rubric fail?
00:06:58 Marcus: Yes — our alert DSL supports AND/OR combinators so you can require multiple conditions, and we support suppression windows.
00:07:06 Priya: Quick pause — any questions about licensing or high-level fit before we go deeper?
00:07:11 Lena: Curious whether Redwood can do per-customer prompt splits — i.e., test candidate only for 10% of users but only those in segment X.
00:07:18 Marcus: Yes — routing policies let you target by header, user ID, geolocation — you can do percent rollouts to a segment.
00:07:24 Danielle: On the eval side, can we run offline A/B that uses real historical traffic so the sample distribution matches production?
00:07:31 Marcus: Absolutely — you can re-play historical sessions, or sample from your event store. We can also run parallel live experiments with traffic mirroring.
00:07:41 00:07:45 Mark: (background noise) Sorry, connection glitch.
00:07:50 Priya: No worries — Marcus, maybe show the drift dashboard with the time series.
00:07:55 Marcus: Opening Time Series -> here's a prompt-level chart for a metric over 30 days. The shaded area is a rolling baseline, the red dots are flagged anomalies. You can click a dot to view raw responses and the diffs.
00:08:12 Marcus: For triage we provide a prioritized list with suggested remediation: revert model, tweak prompt, or run targeted human labeling.
00:08:22 Lena: About human labeling — can Redwood host the labeling or do we need to bring our own?
00:08:27 Marcus: Both. We integrate with managed label providers and also let you bring your own labeling workflow. Labels attach to prompt IDs which helps stable tracking.
00:08:36 Marcus: Now switching to the Optimize recommendations — this is the part that suggests batching and quant settings to hit your latency/cost target for the selected model.
00:08:47 Marcus: You can provide a target like "95th percentile latency < 120ms" and Redwood will give recommended batch sizes, cache timeouts, and quantization profiles and estimate cost savings.
00:08:59 Mark: Is that auto-validated? Like you can run a canary and measure actuals?
00:09:03 Marcus: Yes — we can simulate or run a short canary to validate the recommendations and feed results back into the optimizer.
00:09:10 Priya: Quick security interjection — you mentioned KMS integrations?
00:09:13 Marcus: Yes we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSMs for Private. For hosted we can enable envelope encryption and redact PII before storage. We'll include the security whitepaper.
00:09:25 Danielle: Will you include SOC2 scope?
00:09:27 Priya: We'll send current SOC2 docs and a compliance checklist.
00:09:31 00:09:36 Lena: What about retention windows — we need 90-day access logs and 7-year audit trails for some customers.
00:09:41 Marcus: Retention is configurable in Private; for hosted we have tiers and can export logs to your storage for long-term archival.
00:09:50 Marcus: I'm going to walk through a real regressions workflow now — we had an example where a prompt that used to return a short order summary started truncating and causing higher cart abandonment.
00:09:59 Marcus: Here the A/B shows v1 had 92% pass on the order-summary rubric, v2 dropped to 68%. The system created an 'incident' and suggested rollback. You can click to see affected prompts and raw responses.
00:10:13 00:10:18 Mark: Can we set automatic rollback on severe business-impact regressions?
00:10:21 Marcus: Yes — we map metrics to business-impact tiers, and can auto-fallback to the last known-good model for that route.
00:10:28 Priya: A quick note on provenance — every run includes the model hash, tokenizer version, prompt-set id, and environment so you can reproduce.
00:10:37 Danielle: How does this work with on-prem models?
00:10:40 Marcus: For Private deployments the Eval agent runs inside your network, sends only metadata to the control plane, and you keep raw responses internal.
00:10:48 Marcus: (small demo pause) I'm going to create a custom metric now — a regex-based extraction that counts when responses mention 'promo code' incorrectly.
00:10:58 Marcus: Adding metric -> regex -> sample results. We can set an alert on that metric combined with semantic drop.
00:11:08 Lena: Nice. Can we also tie in user engagement metrics from our product analytics?
00:11:12 Marcus: Yes, you can ingest product telemetry and correlate with eval metrics — e.g., increased cart abandonment correlated with lower 'order-summary' score. We surface correlation coefficients.
00:11:23 Priya: Quick check on integration effort — do you want to run the initial eval with Redwood team help or try self-serve?
00:11:30 Lena: We'd like a joint run. Mark will prep the prompt set and sample traffic, and we want Redwood to help configure alerts for the first run.
00:11:38 Mark: Sounds good. We'll also want an infra session focused on VPC and KMS.
00:11:43 Priya: We'll schedule that.
00:11:46 00:11:50 Marcus: Ok, jumping to the API error modes — note we support structured failure responses and a fallback control plane. You can specify a fallback model or canned response when the primary fails.
00:11:58 Danielle: In case of higher latency we want to respond with a partial result rather than a blank. Can Redwood do streaming partials?
00:12:04 Marcus: Yes — streaming partials and circuit-breaker policies. You can set a latency budget per-route.
00:12:10 Priya: We're about 12 minutes in — maybe we speed through the remaining features and then do Q&A.
00:12:15 Marcus: Sure. I'll highlight the Dashboard export options and the eval-run API payload.
00:12:20 Marcus: Export -> choose fields -> include raw responses and diffs -> create export job. You can store exports to your cloud bucket with connector keys.
00:12:30 00:12:33 Mark: For PII we might prefer redaction hooks before export.
00:12:36 Marcus: We provide pre-export hooks and on-the-fly redaction.
00:12:40 Marcus: Next feature: Regression grouping — related failures are clustered by token-level diffs and rubric mismatches to reduce noise.
00:12:50 Lena: That helps a lot.
00:12:53 Marcus: Now a quick look at the 'A/B drift compare' visualization — side-by-side responses with highlighted diffs and an aggregated lift table.
00:13:03 Marcus: I'll create a synthetic canary to show how we auto-fallback when both semantic and business rubric drop below thresholds. (runs)
00:13:12 00:13:15 Danielle: Can you generate a shareable report for execs that hides prompt-level raws?
00:13:19 Marcus: Yes — we have redact/export templates for executive summaries that show aggregate KPIs and remediation steps without raw user text.
00:13:27 Priya: Time check — about 20 minutes left, let's cover the CI integration and then open to technical Qs.
00:13:35 Marcus: The CI example: webhook trigger on PR -> push prompts to Redwood eval API -> run -> post results back to PR. You can fail the PR if any critical regressed tests.
00:13:47 Mark: We'll want to gate on a small core set of prompts. Do you support multiple prompt tiers?
00:13:52 Marcus: Yes — tag prompts as smoke/core/edge and specify which tiers are run in CI vs nightly.
00:13:59 00:14:02 Lena: Regarding cost — could you give a quick estimate for a 1k prompt offline run?
00:14:06 Priya: Roughly token-cost plus a small processing charge — we'll send an exact estimate post-call once we see average token lengths.
00:14:14 Marcus: Switching to a short live-run example — I'm going to trigger a mirrored run using a small sample of historical traffic.
00:14:22 00:14:30 Marcus: (demo runs) Results: candidate model shows minor lift on NPS-style rubric but regression on 'discount application' mentions. You can drill into affected user segments.
00:14:40 Mark: Ok that's actionable.
00:14:44 Priya: Let's capture the remaining questions so we can follow up.
00:14:48 Danielle: One question on SLA for dedicated instances.
00:14:51 Priya: Dedicated carries SLA commitments; we'll include the SLA doc in the packet.
00:14:56 Lena: Another: how do you handle model version pinning for multi-tenant routes?
00:15:01 Marcus: You can pin per-route or per-customer; routing policies let you constrain model buckets by tenant.
00:15:08 Mark: For Private, what are the minimum infra requirements? GPU counts?
00:15:12 Priya: We'll have Marcus follow up with a sizing guide based on throughput and latency targets.
00:15:18 Marcus: I'll attach a template for the throughput questionnaire.
00:15:22 00:15:30 Lena: Any questions about security from your side?
00:15:32 Priya: Not right now, but we'll send the security packet and SOC2.
00:15:36 Marcus: Wrapping up the demo — the key takeaways: Redwood gives prompt-set driven evals, alerting with combinators, A/B comparisons with raw diffs, CI gating, and options for hosted/dedicated/private with KMS and auditing.
00:15:50 Danielle: Sounds good.
00:15:52 Priya: Next steps recap: we'll provision trial access, Marcus will run an initial bench with Mark's sample prompts, and we'll schedule an infra deep-dive.
00:15:59 Marcus: Also sending the playbook and a sample webhook integration.
00:16:04 Lena: Great, thanks.
00:16:06 00:16:10 Mark: Quick micro-ask — can Marcus include example dashboards so our PMs can look?
00:16:14 Marcus: Yes, will include a link to the exec report template and dashboard screenshots.
00:16:20 Priya: Anything else? If not we'll open for one last question.
00:16:25 Danielle: One last: can Redwood surface which prompts are brittle vs stable over time?
00:16:30 Marcus: Yes — we compute stability scores per prompt and suggest which prompts to seed for human labeling.
00:16:38 00:16:42 Lena: Ok, that's it from us. Thanks for the walkthrough.
00:16:46 Priya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet within 48 hours.
00:16:50 Marcus: Thanks folks.
00:16:55 END OF RECORDING

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription with some speaker mislabels and occasional mis-hearings (e.g., K V cache transcription, "decK" instead of "deck"). References shared: security packet link (will be emailed), demo recording (link to be provided), sample playbook (link to be provided).

Call recap (short): Redwood demoed evaluation tooling: prompt sets, A/B/offline comparisons, regression alerts with combinator logic, CI gating, and optimize recommendations for latency/cost. Customer to provide prompt corpus and schedule infra deep-dive; next deliverables: trial account, security docs, cost estimate, and demo recording.
